pr_title: Defined out MUTEX attributes not available on NonStop SPT Threads.
pr_body:
Standard Posix Threads (SPT) Threads are an older separate branch of
pthreads that do not support some of the capabilities in the current
Posix User Threads (PUT).

Fixes #15885

Signed-off-by: Randall S. Becker <rsbecker@nexbridge.com>
pr_comments: I moved this back from WIP as this fix does solve the two compile issues that showed up. The SPT build is currently under test. If any issues come up, I will open a new case for the specifics after whatever analysis is needed.
This set of changes is kinda gross for a non-supported platform during the beta phase.

> This set of changes is kinda gross for a non-supported platform during the beta phase.

Is it really non-supported? It is a secondary platform, yes, but I would not call that non-supported.
I don't consider this somewhat exotic platform to be project supported.  I.e. it's not primary or secondary as per policy.

> 
> 
> I don't consider this somewhat exotic platform to be project supported. I.e. it's not primary or secondary as per policy.

I'm not sure this discussion belongs here, but I'm wondering why I am putting the effort in, following the discussion I had with the team in the 1.1.x timeframe to bring NonStop back into support (looking for it but it's on an old computer). The consideration was to have a designated person (me as part of my team) who would provide ongoing testing and modification support for the platform. NonStop, while an MPP architecture, is a currently supported platform, by Hewlett Packard Enterprises in a large number of financial, manufacturing, and telco data centres. It is not, nor are there plans, to move the x86 variant operating system to a community supported platform. I have a backup in this activity in case I am unable to continue this role. So if the requirement changes, how can this be rectified? I don't think a simple "Well GitHub doesn't support it" is a sufficient decision point.

Regardless of whether supported or unsupported, given the substantial effort @rsbeckerca spends testing and ensuring the NonStop works with 3.0, I think his work deserves attention and fixes (if approved) being merged before the final release.

The build failure on Windows is _interesting_ and meaning that we have the same redefinition of close on Windows as well although it somehow applies to the declaration as well and so it does not break the build. Hmm, the proper fix might be to rename the `close` member of the struct to something less overloaded.

issue_context.title: OpenSSL-3.0.0-beta1 compile breaks under Standard Posix Threads (NonStop)
issue_context.body:
The definitions associated with the change at lines 60-64 in `crypto/threads_pthread.c` are not defined for all Standard Posix Thread (SPT) implementations.

https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/86ff7cf2a6cdf26f2ba7e64db6fe5c92c64bf9ac/crypto/threads_pthread.c#L60-L64

In particular, `PTHREAD_MUTEX_NORMAL` is undefined. I will look into fixing this ASAP.
comments: I did not catch this earlier because our threaded builds were not working :( and I had an error in our CI pipeline.

So presumably:
```
#ifndef PTHREAD_MUTEX_NORMAL
# define PTHREAD_MUTEX_NORMAL PTHREAD_MUTEX_DEFAULT
#endif
```

> 
> 
> So presumably:
> 
> ```
> #ifndef PTHREAD_MUTEX_NORMAL
> # define PTHREAD_MUTEX_NORMAL PTHREAD_MUTEX_DEFAULT
> #endif
> ```

I don't even have that on the box. Need to define out the whole thing. Problem is that the build is worse than I thought. `netdb.h` is being referenced in multiple places different, that I have to fix as well. OTOH maybe not. I'm rechecking the pipeline.
Looks like it was relatively simple. I tried to document the situation in the code. Still under build/test cycle.

@richsalz I need some help. 
```
          ret = ctx->loader->close(ctx->loader_ctx);
                             ^
"/home/ituglib/randall/openssl-3.0/crypto/store/store_lib.c", line 516: error(1565):
          struct "ossl_store_loader_st" has no field "spt_close"
```
It looks like `close` is redirected to `spt_close`. I'm wondering whether I need to adjust the redirection where `close` is defined.

What I had to do is:
```
    if (ctx->fetched_loader == NULL)
# if defined (OPENSSL_TANDEM_FLOSS) && defined (_SPT_MODEL_)
   /* NonStop SPT redirects close to spt_close causing a compile failure. */
#  undef close
# endif
        ret = ctx->loader->close(ctx->loader_ctx);
# if defined (OPENSSL_TANDEM_FLOSS) && defined (_SPT_MODEL_)
#  define close(filedes) spt_close(filedes)
# endif
```
That undef/redef is bad. It is really depending on the internals of the system header file.  Yuk.

review_comments: Yep, better alternative would be to do here: `# elif defined(PTHREAD_MUTEX_NORMAL)`
@t8m Please have a look at my proposed revision.
Ouch, this looks wrong. This else has to be kept (indented by one space).

What it looks like in my branch:
https://github.com/rsbeckerca/openssl/blob/d453475b2c5456b7631587299955d69a02c36b99/crypto/threads_pthread.c#L60-L67
which puts the `#   else` in the correct place although it looks a little awkward given the code contained.
```
#  if !defined (__TANDEM) && !defined (_SPT_MODEL_)
#   if !defined(NDEBUG) && !defined(OPENSSL_NO_MUTEX_ERRORCHECK)
    pthread_mutexattr_settype(&attr, PTHREAD_MUTEX_ERRORCHECK);
    pthread_mutexattr_settype(&attr, PTHREAD_MUTEX_NORMAL);
#   endif
#  else
    /* The SPT Thread Library does not define MUTEX attributes. */
#  endif
```
This is of course wrong - there is missing `#   else` between the pthread calls.
